subjective: The pet parent reports that Billu is approximately three to four years old. Billu had a previous injury from a car accident, for which a spray was recommended but not applied. The owner is aware of the need for regular flea treatment applications and de-worming every three months. There is mention of some pain at a site where a lesion or issue was removed, and a pre-warming liquid treatment was applied. The owner is concerned about vaccine availability and cost. No other specific symptoms or behavioral changes were reported.
objective: The veterinarian noted a painful area that was treated and removed, with plans for follow-up examination. Pre-warming liquid treatment was applied. De-worming has been done, with instructions for subsequent doses. No other physical examination findings or vital signs were documented in the conversation.
assessment: The patient requires regular flea control and de-worming every three months. There is a history of a pre-cancerous lesion that was removed and treated with a pre-warming liquid. The veterinarian emphasizes the importance of vaccination when available. The previous car accident injury was managed with a recommended spray, though it was not applied initially. The patient is under ongoing monitoring for skin or lesion-related issues.
plan:
1. Administer the available vaccine when possible to provide protection.
2. Continue flea control with monthly spot-on applications (iStick or similar), obtained from veterinary stores or online.
3. Maintain de-worming schedule every three months, with follow-up doses as recommended (next dose within 11 days after initial).
4. Monitor the treated lesion site; follow-up examination planned within three to six months.
5. Avoid bathing Billu for at least 30 minutes after topical treatment application.
6. Prevent Billu from scratching or biting the treated area.
7. Provide prescription for spot-on flea treatment to the owner.
8. Educate owner about possible rare reactions to treatments.
9. Consider re-boarding if needed for additional care.
conclusion: Billu, a three to four-year-old domestic cat, has a history of a pre-cancerous lesion that was removed and treated with a pre-warming liquid. The patient requires regular flea control and de-worming every three months. Vaccination is recommended when the vaccine becomes available. The owner is advised to apply monthly spot-on flea treatments and follow the de-worming schedule. The lesion site will be monitored with follow-up planned in three to six months. Care instructions include avoiding bathing shortly after topical treatments and preventing the cat from scratching the treated area. The previous car accident injury was managed with a recommended spray, though it was not applied initially. Overall, Billu is under ongoing care with preventive and monitoring measures in place.
key_issues:
1. Pre-cancerous lesion removal and treatment - requires monitoring and follow-up.
2. Flea infestation prevention - requires monthly spot-on treatment.
3. De-worming schedule adherence every three months.
4. Vaccination availability and administration.
5. Previous trauma from car accident - managed with topical spray.
abnormal_findings: Painful lesion site that required removal and pre-warming liquid treatment. History of pre-cancerous condition.
customer_instructions:
1. Apply flea control spot-on treatment monthly without fail.
2. Follow de-worming schedule every three months; ensure next dose is given within 11 days after initial.
3. Avoid bathing Billu for at least 30 minutes after applying topical treatments.
4. Prevent Billu from scratching or biting the treated area.
5. Obtain flea treatment products from veterinary medical stores or online.
6. Monitor the lesion site and bring Billu for follow-up examination in three to six months.
7. Administer vaccine when it becomes available.
8. Be aware of possible rare reactions to treatments and report any concerns.
reminders:
1. Follow-up examination of the lesion site in three to six months.
2. Next de-worming dose to be given within 11 days after initial dose.
3. Monthly flea treatment application to be continued regularly.
4. Vaccination to be administered when available.
